editions.text:
The station recorded 19 species and 118 feeder visits, making it the quietest day of the past week compared to the recent average of 266.6 visits. While species diversity matched the weekly mean, the low traffic volume stands out against the heavier counts seen earlier in the period. Most regulars, including Tufted Titmice, Carolina Chickadees, and Northern Cardinals, maintained their consistent presence at the feeders.

Audio detection totaled 367 events, exceeding the weekly average despite the drop in visual visits. Eastern Phoebes and Eastern Towhees accounted for the majority of these detections.

Two raptors, a Red-shouldered Hawk and an American Kestrel, were heard during the day, both of which have been present at the station in the recent past. The Pileated Woodpecker was also detected, continuing its intermittent appearances. No new species were recorded visually or audibly that were not previously established at this station, maintaining the known baseline of local avian residents.
